question: A market research team has Claude summarise findings from six regional reports and now wants a final recommendation. Which two things should they do before asking for that recommendation? Select two.
options: A) Agree the criteria the recommendation will be judged on, such as cost, risk and timing.
B) Check the summarised findings against the reports so the next step builds on solid ground.
C) Paste all six original reports back in again so nothing at all can have been left out.
D) Ask for three alternative recommendations at once and pick whichever one reads strongest.
E) Move to a faster response setting, since the remaining step is short and mostly writing.
correct_answers: A) Agree the criteria the recommendation will be judged on, such as cost, risk and timing.
B) Check the summarised findings against the reports so the next step builds on solid ground.
explanations: Correct. This is an independent point about specification rather than verification: without stated criteria, the recommendation cannot be argued for or assessed.
Correct. The recommendation inherits every error in the summary stage. Verifying the intermediate output is what makes decomposition safer than one long prompt.
Re-pasting the full reports discards the work already done and pushes the team back to the single overloaded request that decomposition was meant to avoid.
Choosing on how a draft reads substitutes fluency for judgment, and none of the three options has been measured against anything the team actually cares about.
The final step is the judgment-heavy one, so speed is the wrong thing to optimise for here, and it does nothing about unverified inputs.
